# Rules

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs` from src/rules. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every finding is a **review prompt**, not a verdict. Weakening a test is sometimes the right call because the spec changed. goalposts makes sure a human decides.

Silence one line with a comment `goalposts-ignore: GP002` on or directly above it. Silence a rule everywhere with `"ignore": ["GP002"]` in `.goalposts.json`, or change its level with `"severity": { "GP005": "low" }`.

| ID | Name | Default | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| [GP001](#gp001) | test-file-deleted | high | A test file was deleted. |
| [GP002](#gp002) | test-skipped | high | A test was skipped, marked expected-to-fail, focused with .only, or commented out. |
| [GP003](#gp003) | assertion-removed | high | Assertions were deleted without replacement. |
| [GP004](#gp004) | assertion-loosened | high | An exact-value assertion was replaced by an existence or truthiness check. |
| [GP005](#gp005) | expected-value-changed | medium | An assertion kept its shape but its literal values changed. |
| [GP006](#gp006) | test-case-removed | medium | A test case was deleted from a file that still exists. |
| [GP007](#gp007) | error-swallowed | medium | A test now ignores errors (empty catch, `except: pass`). |
| [GP008](#gp008) | snapshot-rewritten | medium | Existing snapshot content was rewritten. |
| [GP009](#gp009) | flakiness-masked | low | Retries, reruns or a flaky marker were added to tests. |
| [GP010](#gp010) | trivial-assertion | high | An assertion that can never fail was added. |
| [GP020](#gp020) | check-suppressed | low | Lint, type or coverage suppressions were added. |
| [GP030](#gp030) | ci-gate-weakened | high | A CI or script check can now fail silently, or a check step was removed. |
| [GP031](#gp031) | threshold-or-strictness-lowered | high | A coverage threshold was lowered, or strictness (types, lint, warnings) was relaxed. |
| [GP032](#gp032) | test-selection-narrowed | medium | The test command or runner config now runs fewer tests, or the test script changed. |
| [GP040](#gp040) | hardcoded-to-test | high | New source code special-cases a literal that a test asserts. |
| [GP041](#gp041) | test-environment-detection | high | Non-test code was changed to behave differently when tests are running. |
| [GP100](#gp100) | base-tests-fail-on-head | high | The original tests fail against the new code, but pass once the modified tests are used. |

## GP001

**test-file-deleted** · default severity **high**

A test file was deleted.

*Why it matters:* Deleting a failing test file is the quickest way to get a green run. It is fine when the code it covered was deleted too.

- Flagged: `git rm tests/test_cart.py` while `cart.py` stays
- Not flagged: deleting `cart.py` and its test together

## GP002

**test-skipped** · default severity **high**

A test was skipped, marked expected-to-fail, focused with .only, or commented out.

*Why it matters:* A skipped test cannot fail. The suite stays green while the behaviour it checked goes unverified.

- Flagged: `+ @pytest.mark.skip`, `+ it.only(`, `+ t.Skip()`, `- assert x` → `+ # assert x`
- Not flagged: a skip that was already there

## GP003

**assertion-removed** · default severity **high**

Assertions were deleted without replacement.

*Why it matters:* A test with fewer assertions checks less. Removing the one that failed is a common way to turn a red run green.

- Flagged: `- expect(total).toBe(42)` with no replacement
- Not flagged: the same assertion moved to another file

## GP004

**assertion-loosened** · default severity **high**

An exact-value assertion was replaced by an existence or truthiness check.

*Why it matters:* `toBe(42)` becoming `toBeTruthy()` still runs, still looks like a test, and no longer pins any behaviour.

- Flagged: `- expect(x).toBe(42)` → `+ expect(x).toBeTruthy()`
- Not flagged: `toBe(42)` → `toBe(43)` (that is GP005)

## GP005

**expected-value-changed** · default severity **medium**

An assertion kept its shape but its literal values changed.

*Why it matters:* Sometimes the spec really changed. Sometimes the code is wrong and the expectation was edited to match its output. Only a human can tell which.

- Flagged: `- assertEqual(f(2), 4)` → `+ assertEqual(f(2), 5)`
- Not flagged: adding a new assertion

## GP006

**test-case-removed** · default severity **medium**

A test case was deleted from a file that still exists.

*Why it matters:* A deleted case cannot fail. Check that the behaviour it covered is gone or covered elsewhere.

- Flagged: a `def test_x` removed from a file that still exists
- Not flagged: renaming a test

## GP007

**error-swallowed** · default severity **medium**

A test now ignores errors (empty catch, `except: pass`).

*Why it matters:* A test that swallows exceptions passes whether or not the code under test throws.

- Flagged: `+ except Exception: pass` in a test, `+ .catch(() => {})`
- Not flagged: try/except around cleanup in non-test code

## GP008

**snapshot-rewritten** · default severity **medium**

Existing snapshot content was rewritten.

*Why it matters:* Updating a snapshot makes the test pass by definition. Whether the new output is right needs a human read.

- Flagged: `__snapshots__/a.snap` changed lines
- Not flagged: a brand-new snapshot file

## GP009

**flakiness-masked** · default severity **low**

Retries, reruns or a flaky marker were added to tests.

*Why it matters:* Retrying until green hides real intermittent failures such as races.

- Flagged: `+ jest.retryTimes(3)`, `+ @pytest.mark.flaky`
- Not flagged: retries that were already configured

## GP010

**trivial-assertion** · default severity **high**

An assertion that can never fail was added.

*Why it matters:* `assert True` and `expect(true).toBe(true)` raise the test count and the coverage number while verifying nothing.

- Flagged: `+ assert True`, `+ expect(true).toBe(true)`
- Not flagged: real assertions

## GP020

**check-suppressed** · default severity **low**

Lint, type or coverage suppressions were added.

*Why it matters:* Each `# type: ignore` or `eslint-disable` silences a checker instead of fixing what it found. A few are normal; a burst in one change deserves a look.

- Flagged: `+ // @ts-ignore`, `+ # type: ignore`, `+ // eslint-disable-next-line`
- Not flagged: one pre-existing suppression left untouched

## GP030

**ci-gate-weakened** · default severity **high**

A CI or script check can now fail silently, or a check step was removed.

*Why it matters:* `continue-on-error: true`, `|| true` and deleted lint/test steps turn a gate into a suggestion.

- Flagged: `+ continue-on-error: true`, `+ npm test || true`, `- run: npm run lint`
- Not flagged: a step that is reworded but still runs the same command

## GP031

**threshold-or-strictness-lowered** · default severity **high**

A coverage threshold was lowered, or strictness (types, lint, warnings) was relaxed.

*Why it matters:* Lowering `fail_under` or switching `strict` off moves the finish line instead of reaching it.

- Flagged: `fail_under = 90` → `70`, `"strict": true` → `false`, a lint rule set to `"off"`
- Not flagged: raising a threshold

## GP032

**test-selection-narrowed** · default severity **medium**

The test command or runner config now runs fewer tests, or the test script changed.

*Why it matters:* Excluding paths, deselecting tests or replacing the `test` script keeps the run green by running less.

- Flagged: `"test": "jest"` → `"test": "echo ok"`, `+ --deselect tests/x.py`
- Not flagged: adding flags to the test script that do not exclude tests

## GP040

**hardcoded-to-test** · default severity **high**

New source code special-cases a literal that a test asserts.

*Why it matters:* `if (input == "the test value") return expected` passes the test without implementing the behaviour. It is the oldest trick in test-gaming and agents reproduce it.

- Flagged: `+ if (x === 1234.56) return 246.91;` where a test asserts `1234.56`
- Not flagged: a new constant no test mentions

## GP041

**test-environment-detection** · default severity **high**

Non-test code was changed to behave differently when tests are running.

*Why it matters:* Code that checks `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` or `NODE_ENV === "test"` can pass tests by taking a different path from production.

- Flagged: `+ if os.environ.get("PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST"):` in application code
- Not flagged: the same check inside a test helper

## GP100

**base-tests-fail-on-head** · only produced with `--verify "<command>"`

The original tests fail against the new code, but pass once the modified tests are used.

*Why it matters:* This is direct evidence, not a heuristic: the code does not satisfy the tests that existed before the change.

goalposts copies your project into two temporary directories, runs your command in the first as-is, then restores the pre-change version of every modified or deleted test file in the second and runs it again. If the first passes and the second fails, the change only looks green because the tests moved. Dependency folders (`node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `vendor`) are symlinked, not copied. Your working tree is never modified.

## What goalposts does not do

- It does not run an LLM and makes no network calls.
- It cannot judge whether a new expectation is *correct*; it can only show you that it changed.
- Semantic cheating that leaves no textual trace (for example, mocking out the unit under test in a brand-new test) is outside what a diff scan can see.
